observation.visible_scene: A workshop with a dark brick wall, a metal drum on the left, and a vertical power hammer (drop forge) in the center. A man in a grey shirt and a yellow protective glove stands at the machine, holding a glowing orange-hot metal billet on the anvil/die with long tongs. The hammer's cylindrical ram/tool hangs above the workpiece, which stays incandescent throughout.
visible_changes: The hammer ram's vertical position relative to the workpiece varies across the frames: it sits lower/closer to the glowing billet in some frames (around the middle of the clip) and is raised again in others, consistent with the machine cycling/striking the work.
The smith's gloved hand and tongs shift slightly, repositioning/rotating the glowing billet on the die.
The billet remains bright orange-hot on the anvil the whole time.
The smith's head and torso posture change subtly as he leans over and watches/adjusts the work.
Background elements (brick wall, drum, machine body) stay fixed, indicating the camera is essentially static.
outside_clip_unknowns: The heating of the billet before this segment and its final forged shape/outcome after it are not shown.
Whether each ram descent is a full strike or a partial compression is not fully determinable from the sampled frames.
uncertain_details: Exact timing and count of hammer strikes between sampled frames.
Precise amount of camera motion (background evidence suggests it is negligible but not absolutely certain).
The exact material identity of the glowing piece.
